# ca

```go
import "github.com/effective-security/trustyca/internal/ca"
```

Package ca is the core of the Certification Authority: it resolves the issuer and the profile that serve a tenant request, builds authority issuers from the issuer rows and their keys, creates and imports issuers, and mirrors the platform ca\-config into the CA tables.

The Registry is the entry point of the signing services. Every lookup names its tenant scope and the built issuers are cached by row ID, so the labels of different orgs and projects never collide \(DESIGN.md sections 5 and 6\):

```
keys := ca.NewKeys(cryptoProviders, dataProtection)
registry := ca.NewRegistry(caDb, keys, ca.Options{TTL: 5 * time.Minute})

res, err := registry.Resolve(ctx, &ca.ResolveRequest{
	OrgID:     orgID,
	ProjectID: projectID,
	Profile:   "server",
})
if err != nil {
	// errors.Is(err, ca.ErrProfileNotFound), ca.ErrIssuerNotFound, ...
}
crt, pem, err := res.Issuer.Sign(csr.SignRequest{
	Request: csrPEM,
	Profile: res.ProfileName,
})
```

Keys generates the key of a new issuer in a crypto provider, or wraps a software key with the data protection provider, and loads the key of a row; NewRootIssuer, NewSignedIssuer, NewPendingIssuer, ImportIssuer and ActivatedIssuer build the rows the service registers. Registry.Bootstrap registers the platform issuers, roots and profiles of an authority.Config at startup and loads the enabled issuers, so that one that does not load fails the start.

## Constants

<a name="SoftwareKeyProvider"></a>

```go
const (
    // SoftwareKeyProvider names the provider of a key that no crypto
    // provider holds: the key material is kept wrapped by the data
    // protection provider in key_protected. It is the name of the xpki
    // in-memory provider, which generates such keys and is for tests and
    // development only.
    SoftwareKeyProvider = "inmem"

    // DefaultKeyAlgo is the algorithm of a generated key when the request
    // names none
    DefaultKeyAlgo = "ECDSA"
    // DefaultKeySize is the curve of a generated key when the request names
    // none
    DefaultKeySize = 256
)
```

<a name="DefaultCacheTTL"></a>

```go
const (
    // DefaultCacheTTL bounds the staleness of the cached issuers and
    // profiles when the configuration sets none: a change made by another
    // instance is visible within five minutes (DESIGN.md section 5.1)
    DefaultCacheTTL = 5 * time.Minute
    // DefaultCacheSize is the number of issuers kept in memory when the
    // configuration sets none
    DefaultCacheSize = 1000
)
```

## Variables

<a name="ErrProfileNotFound"></a>Errors of the issuer and profile resolution. They are returned wrapped with a stack, so compare them with errors.Is; the service maps them to its status codes.

```go
var (
    // ErrProfileNotFound is returned when the scope has no active profile
    // with the label, in the project or in the org
    ErrProfileNotFound = errors.New("profile not found")
    // ErrIssuerNotFound is returned when the scope has no issuer with the
    // label, in the project or in the org
    ErrIssuerNotFound = errors.New("issuer not found")
    // ErrIssuerNotActive is returned when the issuer exists but does not
    // sign: it is Pending, Archived or Destroyed
    ErrIssuerNotActive = errors.New("issuer is not active")
    // ErrIssuerLabelRequired is returned when the profile binds to any
    // issuer and the request names none
    ErrIssuerLabelRequired = errors.New("issuer label is required")
    // ErrIssuerMismatch is returned when the request names an issuer other
    // than the one the profile binds to
    ErrIssuerMismatch = errors.New("issuer does not match the profile")
    // ErrProfileNotAllowed is returned when a profile bound to any issuer is
    // not listed in the AllowedProfiles of the issuer
    ErrProfileNotAllowed = errors.New("issuer does not allow the profile")
    // ErrIssuerExpired is returned when the certificate of the issuer is no
    // longer valid, so it signs no CRL
    ErrIssuerExpired = errors.New("issuer certificate has expired")
    // ErrSoftwareKeysDisabled is returned by Keys when a key that no crypto
    // provider holds (a key the inmem provider generates, a PEM key of an
    // import or of a bootstrap key file) is refused: the configuration
    // allows keys of the crypto providers only (ca.allow_software_keys)
    ErrSoftwareKeysDisabled = errors.New("software keys are not allowed: use a key of a crypto provider")
)
```

<a name="LoadBootstrapConfig"></a>
## func [LoadBootstrapConfig](<https://github.com/effective-security/trustyca/blob/main/internal/ca/bootstrap.go#L38>)

```go
func LoadBootstrapConfig(path string) (*authority.Config, error)
```

LoadBootstrapConfig loads the ca\-config of the platform bootstrap with authority.LoadConfig, which expands \`$VAR\` and \`$\{VAR\}\` as environment variables in every value: a \`$\{ISSUER\_ID\}\` in the AIA, CRL or OCSP URL template of an issuer would become an empty string, and every certificate the issuer signs would name the URL without the issuer. A file whose templates name the issuer that way is refused before it is loaded; file issuers use pbconv.IssuerIDPlaceholder \(\`:ISSUER\_ID\`\).

<a name="SubjectKeyID"></a>
## func [SubjectKeyID](<https://github.com/effective-security/trustyca/blob/main/internal/ca/keys.go#L394>)

```go
func SubjectKeyID(pub crypto.PublicKey) (string, error)
```

SubjectKeyID returns the key identifier of a public key: the SHA\-1 of its subjectPublicKey bits \(RFC 5280 section 4.2.1.2 method 1\). It is the identifier the CA puts in the certificates it issues, the IKID of the certificates the key signs and the issuer key hash of their OCSP requests, so a Pending issuer is identified by it before it has a certificate.

<a name="CrlPublisher"></a>
## type [CrlPublisher](<https://github.com/effective-security/trustyca/blob/main/internal/ca/crl.go#L56-L59>)

CrlPublisher signs and stores the CRLs of the issuers \(DESIGN.md section 8\). The PublishCrls method of the CA service and the crl\_renewal task share it: a CRL is published when the issuer has none, when the current one is within the renewal period of its next update, or on demand. The CRL number is the issuer's current number plus one, and db.PublishCrl stores the CRL and the number in one transaction, refusing a number that is not greater than the issuer's: when another instance publishes first, the CRL is signed again with the next number.

A CrlPublisher is safe for concurrent use.

```go
type CrlPublisher struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="CrlPublisher.PublishCrl"></a>
### func \(\*CrlPublisher\) [PublishCrl](<https://github.com/effective-security/trustyca/blob/main/internal/ca/crl.go#L202>)

```go
func (p *CrlPublisher) PublishCrl(ctx context.Context, row *model.Issuer, force bool) (*model.Crl, bool, error)
```

PublishCrl signs and stores the CRL of the issuer row when it is due \(CrlDue with the renewal period of the issuer settings\), or when forced, and returns the CRL and true. When the current CRL \(db.GetCrl\) is not due it is returned with false. The row must be an Active or Archived issuer whose certificate is valid; its CRL number is the current one, so the row comes from the DB, not from a cache.

<a name="CrlPublisher.PublishCrls"></a>
### func \(\*CrlPublisher\) [PublishCrls](<https://github.com/effective-security/trustyca/blob/main/internal/ca/crl.go#L107>)

```go
func (p *CrlPublisher) PublishCrls(ctx context.Context, req *PublishCrlsRequest) (*PublishCrlsResult, error)
```

PublishCrls publishes the due CRLs of the Active and Archived issuers of the scope, every CRL when forced. The current CRLs of a page of issuers are read in one query \(db.GetCrls\), and an issuer whose CRL is not due is skipped from the settings of its row, before its signer is loaded. An issuer that fails does not stop the run: the failure is logged and counted. The error is a failure to list the issuers or to read their CRLs; the CRLs published before it are in the result.

```go
type ImportRequest struct {
```

<a name="IssuerRequest"></a>
## type [IssuerRequest](<https://github.com/effective-security/trustyca/blob/main/internal/ca/issuer.go#L25-L46>)

IssuerRequest describes an issuer to create: its scope and identity, the key to generate and its runtime settings \(DESIGN.md section 5.2\). The certificate request is built from Subject, SAN and Extensions.

```go
type IssuerRequest struct {
    // OrgID is the owning org; zero is the platform
    OrgID xdb.ID
    // ProjectID is the owning project; zero is the org scope
    ProjectID xdb.ID
    // Label of the issuer, unique in its scope
    Label string
    // Type of the authority
    Type pb.AuthorityType_Enum
    // Subject of the issuer certificate; a common name or names are required
    Subject *csr.X509Subject
    // SAN of the issuer certificate
    SAN []string
    // Extensions of the issuer certificate
    Extensions []csr.X509Extension
    // KeySpec of the key to generate; nil takes the defaults
    KeySpec *pb.KeySpec
    // Provider generates and holds the key
    Provider cryptoprov.Provider
    // Config provides the runtime settings of the issuer
    Config *pb.IssuerConfig
}
```

```go
func (k *Keys) Destroy(_ context.Context, m *model.Issuer) error
```

<a name="Keys.DisableSoftwareKeys"></a>
### func \(\*Keys\) [DisableSoftwareKeys](<https://github.com/effective-security/trustyca/blob/main/internal/ca/keys.go#L143>)

```go
func (k *Keys) DisableSoftwareKeys()
```

DisableSoftwareKeys refuses, with ErrSoftwareKeysDisabled, every key that no crypto provider holds: a key the inmem provider generates, the PEM key of an import and the key file of a bootstrap issuer, which would be stored wrapped in key\_protected. A production configuration disables them \(ca.allow\_software\_keys\), so that every issuer key lives in a KMS or an HSM; the wrapped keys of existing rows still load.

```go
func (k *Keys) NewSignedIssuer(ctx context.Context, req *IssuerRequest, parent *Resolution) (*model.Issuer, error)
```

NewSignedIssuer generates the key of an issuer in the provider and has the parent sign its certificate with the CA profile the parent resolved. The row is Active, with the parent as its parent, the parent and its chain as its chain and the parent's root as its root. A Root is refused: it is self\-signed by NewRootIssuer. The chain of the parent must allow a subordinate CA with the path length of the profile \(checkPathLength\), or the certificates the subordinate issues would never verify.

<a name="Registry"></a>
## type [Registry](<https://github.com/effective-security/trustyca/blob/main/internal/ca/registry.go#L69-L83>)

Registry resolves the issuer and the profile that serve a tenant request and keeps the built authority issuers in memory.

Every lookup names its tenant scope: a label resolves in the project, then in the org, never in the platform or in another org \(DESIGN.md section 6\), and the DB finds rows by exact scope. The built issuers are cached by row ID, which is unique across orgs, so equal labels of different orgs or projects never collide; the resolutions of a scope and label are cached under the requested scope. Both caches are bounded by size and TTL, and a mutation made through this instance invalidates its entries at once \(InvalidateIssuer, InvalidateProfile\); a mutation made by another instance is visible after the TTL. Resolutions that fail are not cached.

A Registry is safe for concurrent use.

```go
type Registry struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="NewRegistry"></a>
### func [NewRegistry](<https://github.com/effective-security/trustyca/blob/main/internal/ca/registry.go#L129>)

```go
func NewRegistry(caDb db.CaReadonlyDb, keys *Keys, opts Options) *Registry
```

NewRegistry returns a registry over the CA tables and the key management

<a name="Registry.Bootstrap"></a>
### func \(\*Registry\) [Bootstrap](<https://github.com/effective-security/trustyca/blob/main/internal/ca/bootstrap.go#L108>)

```go
func (r *Registry) Bootstrap(ctx context.Context, caDb db.CaDb, cfg *authority.Config) (*BootstrapResult, error)
```

Bootstrap mirrors the issuers, trust anchors and profiles of a ca\-config into the platform rows \(org\_id IS NULL\), so that the platform issuers sign tenant CA certificates and CIS serves their chains from the same tables \(DESIGN.md section 5.1\), then loads every enabled issuer, so that a key that does not load or a delegated OCSP profile that does not bind fails the start instead of the first request.

It is idempotent: a registered issuer with the same certificate only has its runtime settings refreshed, roots are registered by thumbprint and profiles are replaced by label. It is also safe when several instances start against one fresh DB at once: an issuer insert that loses the race to another instance continues with the row that instance registered. The key of an issuer is a key URI, stored as the reference, or key material, stored wrapped; both are checked against the certificate. An issuer whose certificate is for a new key is an error: renewal keeps the label unique, so the old issuer must be archived under another label first. A certificate renewed for the registered key is an error too: renewal means a new key, so two certificates never share a SKID \(DESIGN.md section 5.4\). A disabled issuer is archived, so that it stops signing on every instance, and enabled again when the configuration enables it; a destroyed one has no key and is an error. The anchor of a root issuer is written in the transaction of the issuer insert, and registered again on every start from the stored certificate, which restores an anchor that was deleted or that a version without the transaction failed to write.

<a name="Registry.IssuerByKeyHash"></a>
### func \(\*Registry\) [IssuerByKeyHash](<https://github.com/effective-security/trustyca/blob/main/internal/ca/registry.go#L292>)

```go
func (r *Registry) IssuerByKeyHash(ctx context.Context, alg crypto.Hash, hash []byte) (*authority.Issuer, *model.Issuer, error)
```

IssuerByKeyHash returns the issuer whose public key has the hash, as an OCSP request identifies it. The issuers in memory are matched for any algorithm; a SHA\-1 hash is also the Subject Key Identifier of a CA certificate this CA issued \(RFC 5280 method 1\), so it is looked up in the DB. A certificate of an issuer that is not in memory and whose key identifier is not its SHA\-1 key hash is not found.
